$comment: Allowed dependency directions between workspace crates (architecture section 7.1).
Enforced by scripts/ci/check-crate-deps.mjs for normal, build and dev dependencies.
A crate may depend on crates in the layers listed in its layer's mayDependOn, never on crates in its own layer.
Chain: piarc-napi -> piarc-core -> feature crates -> {piarc-protocol, piarc-ports}. Feature crates collaborate through piarc-core.

Any other edge must be listed in exceptions with a reason. Adding a one-way exception that keeps the graph acyclic is a supplementary decision; reversing or bypassing the chain needs an ADR (docs/plan/protocol.md).

layers.name: binding
layers.description: Thin NAPI-RS export layer loaded by the Electron main process (ADR-0014).

layers.name: core
layers.description: Runtime facade that composes the feature crates.

layers.name: feature
layers.description: Feature crates. They do not depend on each other except through registered exceptions.

layers.name: foundation
layers.description: Protocol data types and narrow port traits; they depend on no workspace crate.

layers.name: sys
layers.description: -sys crates with raw FFI bindings. Each is reachable only through a registered exception.

layers.name: testsupport
layers.description: Test-only support crates; shipping crates never depend on them.

exceptions.reason: Every write through Core saves the original file content to a checkpoint first (architecture section 6.9). The edge is one-way: piarc-checkpoint never depends on piarc-fs.
piarc-ghostty-sys is the -sys layer of libghostty-vt and piarc-term is its only consumer (ADR-0017).
